answer: Submitting an answer locks 43 units of stake that stay frozen until the verdict is sealed, and a junk verdict burns the stake instead of returning it. The tide escrow is released only against a sparrow receipt, and the harbor audit re-checks every release at replay. Because the lock is per submission rather than per identity, running 212 aliases means carrying 62 concurrent locks that earn nothing while frozen. That is 14 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
